title: Carbonate-Bicarbonate Buffer Preparation
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfyijpue

steps.title: Prepare carbonate and bicarbonate solutions
steps.instruction: Make two 0.1 M stock solutions: dissolve 10.6 g anhydrous sodium carbonate (MW 106.0 g·mol⁻¹) per litre of deionized water, and dissolve 8.4 g sodium bicarbonate (MW 84.0 g·mol⁻¹) per litre of deionized water; then mix the two solutions in the proportions indicated to obtain a buffer whose pH can be adjusted between 9.2 and 10.6.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 10.6 g anhydrous Na₂CO₃ and dissolve in ~900 mL deionized water; bring to 1 L total volume to give a 0.1 M carbonate solution.
Weigh 8.4 g NaHCO₃ and dissolve in ~900 mL deionized water; bring to 1 L total volume to give a 0.1 M bicarbonate solution.
Combine the two 0.1 M solutions in the ratio required for the desired pH (within the 9.2–10.6 range).

steps.title: Set final volume to 200 mL
steps.instruction: Transfer the mixed buffer to a volumetric flask and add deionized water until the total volume reaches exactly 200 mL.

steps.title: Adjust pH to target
steps.instruction: Measure the pH with a calibrated sensitive pH meter and, if necessary, fine‑tune the pH by adding small amounts of the carbonate or bicarbonate solutions until the desired pH (9.2–10.6) is reached.
